authority_resolution.controlling_scientific_source: peer-reviewed journal article PDF served by the NIST local-download endpoint

journal_pdf_result.locator: PDF page 27, equation (64); also abstract on PDF page 1

authority_resolution.reason: The NIST landing-page abstract displays a numerical final result inconsistent with the peer-reviewed article PDF. This audit does not use landing-page numerical values.

not_uniquely_specified_in_primary_paper.observation: epsilon_j is described as measurement error whose typical size comes from the uncertainty budget, but the probability distribution/likelihood for epsilon is not explicitly stated in the consensus-model section.
not_uniquely_specified_in_primary_paper.promotion: required for unique deterministic reproduction of the posterior

not_uniquely_specified_in_primary_paper.observation: The paper says the model was calibrated using a Bayesian procedure and cites references, but does not specify the paper-specific sampler/integration algorithm.
not_uniquely_specified_in_primary_paper.promotion: required unless an analytic posterior construction is supplied

not_uniquely_specified_in_primary_paper.observation: The paper says 'large samples' from the posterior but does not state a sample count, random seed, burn-in/warmup, thinning, chains, or convergence criterion.
Huber's M and Qn are named and referenced, but the paper does not state all implementation/tuning conventions used on the posterior samples.
not_uniquely_specified_in_primary_paper.promotion: required for unique reproduction of the exact published summaries unless a canonical convention is source-authorized

not_uniquely_specified_in_primary_paper.observation: The consensus paragraph refers to a correlation matrix R in Sigma_ij = tau_i tau_j R_ij. Its identification with the experimental Table 18 correlation matrix is strongly suggested by local context but is not explicitly labeled as 'Table 18' in the equation paragraph.
not_uniquely_specified_in_primary_paper.promotion: must be explicit before claiming exact reproduction of the dark-uncertainty covariance

published_table_19.role: comparison/diagnostic output of the Bayesian model, not an input for deciding reconstructability

specified.consensus_location_summary: Huber's M applied to large samples from posterior(mu)
specified.consensus_uncertainty_summary: Qn applied to large samples from posterior(mu)
specified.lambda_summary: Huber's M estimates from posterior samples

epistemic_limits: No raw NIST PDF bytes are committed or hash-attested in this artifact.
The transcription was reviewed against both machine-readable PDF text and visual page screenshots for Tables 16, 17, 18, 19 and equation (64).
This attestation does not authorize a BIPM-14 versus NIST-26 common-constant conclusion.
It does not authorize replacing the Bayesian hierarchy with generalized least squares and calling the result equation (64).

paper_statements.claim: Several input variables enter more than one measurement, so the four resulting measured values of G are correlated; the corresponding correlation coefficients are listed in Table 18.
paper_statements.locator: PDF page 25, text immediately after Table 16

paper_statements.claim: All correlation coefficients are positive because dominant uncertainty contributions enter with the same sign for all four determinations.

table_16.caption_role: four individual G determinations with combined relative uncertainties (k=1)

table_18.caption_role: summary of relative uncertainties and correlations for the four G determinations
table_18.precision_policy: Table 18 diagonal values control covariance construction because they are the more precise source-reported standard uncertainties; Table 16 whole-ppm values are retained as rounded display records.

source.publication: Stephan Schlamminger et al., Redetermination of the gravitational constant with the BIPM torsion balance at NIST
